Executive Summary

The screenless wearables is the fastest growing sub-category in smart wearables [1], with whoop nearly doubling its revenue ,101% to approx $1.1B [2] and tripling its valuation from $3.6B to $10.1B [3] in FY-25, on the top of the game. India had no brand focusing on proper screenless fitness wearables category, until Noise launched its REP band can this broader this small category or be a part of the “graveyard of wearables”. Let's discuss it with what has Noise working in its favour and what can be improved in the REP band as a product. Tech and value wise. A PRODUCT MANAGEMENT CASE STUDY.

Describe the product

Noise Rep is a “screenless” fitness tracker [4] unlike smartwatches like Garmin and Apple watch, screenless trackers looks just like a band that can be worn on wrist, biceps, even in underwear [5], that continuously tracks body health metrics through sensors. And using these sensor-derived data, they apply complex algorithms to give metrics like Sleep score, Strain, Calories burned, Recovery score, Vo2 max etc.

Problem Statement

NOISE has launched a most expected in indian fitness market product, a Screenless fitness tracker [6], but the category has big and established players such as Google’s Fitbit Air [7], Amazfit’s Helio strap [8], Whoop band [9] which is the industry leader in screenless wearable space and the newly launched Garmin’s Cirqa [10].

With competition already offering advanced health tracking, workout and recovery insights, REP needs to establish a clear reason for users to choose it over the existing alternatives.

This case study explores : What does Noise REP already have working in its favour that can make the product an “Indian” celebrated success in this space, and where does it fall short against its competitors, and what product, technology and value improvements will make Noise a strong pick for its target users?

User Needs & Jobs-to-be-Done

From the above 6 personas, the buying motivation is consolidated in roughly four real jobs for what people are buying A screenless tracker for:

  1. Build for my sport, not for the average user showoff - Himanshu and Aniket — Training specific accuracy like Hyrox and workout load tracking matters more than just general wellness tracking.
  1. Give me clinical-grade data I can act on, with someone that has the metrics knowledge - Suresh — Accuracy matters more for Suresh because of old age and a doctor/expert is the one reading the data, not just him.
  1. Help me act on my numbers without becoming a data expert - Ramesh and Ramya — both want simple, accurate tracking of sleep and general health without a complex UI or having to interpret raw metrics themselves, they need a virtual coach to do it for them and advice based on their numbers.
  1. Let me track my fitness without announcing that I’m tracking fitness - Rahul — The pain point is not the metric, it’s the visibility Rahul wants the device to disappear physically and socially ( Arm band, waist)

REP’s current spec sheet which is ₹10,000 [18], India availability, and no subscription caters partially to job 1(except the no Hyrox mode) and partially to job 3( except the personalised AI coach) and partially to job 4 if Noise decides to launch Arm/waist strap for REP. otherwise job 2, and other real gaps are covered in detail in the below section.

Stage of user journeyWhat REP does wellGaps/ Pain Points

Hardware/ data transparency—Noise does not directly mention their sensors used and the sampling rates for their PPG optical sensors. Which will create a major trust deficit for users like Himanshu and Suresh

REP wins on accessibility and pricing — job 1,3 and 4 partially. But is currently the weakest device in the set for data completeness(SpO2) and transparency( missing sensor and sampling rate data).

Which is where the next section should focus.

Conclusion

Noise REP’s core bet — which is Official India retail, no subscription, and a familiar Whoop like form factor – already solves for the accessibility part of the the problem in the Indian market as Amazfit, Garmin, Fitbit air and Whoop MG is not available in India through official channels currently. Which leaves buyers to depend on amazon usa import or resellers that are selling the device for at least 50% more price.

But REP currently loses on the trust half : An unlaunched SpO2 feature, undisclosed sampling rates, sensor information, no personalised AI coach and no bicep bands/ accessories Unlike the competitors who fulfills most of these at or before launch.

The path forward is not more hardware or multiple features — It’s finishing and being honest about what is already built in the order or : transparency first, data completeness second, engagement features third. If Noise sequences in this way, REP has a shot at becoming the value and segment leader in India’s screenless tracker category rather than being in the “graveyard of wearables”. REP is an unfinished product with a lot of potential.
